newsitem.title: INDIA: India's rulers, Congress to meet again on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: India's rulers, Congress to meet again on Thursday.

text.p: India's ruling coalition and the Congress party on Wednesday adjourned talks for the night, and a Congress negotiator said he was hopeful the two sides would resolve a political crisis threatening the government.

"We are hopeful that we will come to an agreement," Congress negotiator Jitendra Prasad told reporters after the two sides broke off for the night. United Front negotiator Chandrababu Naidu said the talks would resume on Thursday morning.
"We will have further discussions. We will try to resolve the crisis," Naidu said, adding that the talks, which he called cordial, were set to resume on Thursday at 9:30 a.m. (0400 GMT).
The two sides started the talks earlier on Thursday in an effort to resolve the political crisis before a vote of confidence in parliament set for Friday.
Congress triggered the crisis on March 30 when it withdrew support from Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 15-party coalition government.
Congress president Sitaram Kesri has demanded that Deve Gowda step down, but he has refused.
